summary: zenodo-package/upload.ps1 used HTTP POST to the Zenodo bucket URL. Zenodo now rejects POST with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed; bucket uploads require PUT. This blocked the entire upload for days under the mistaken belief it was only a server outage.
what_went_wrong: The upload script was written against the older Zenodo bucket API (POST /api/files/{bucket}/{filename}). The current API requires PUT to the same URL. Every attempt returned 405, which was conflated with the earlier 504 Gateway Timeout outage.
detection: Resumed the aborted upload after the outage; a single-file POST test returned HTTP 405. A PUT test returned HTTP 201 immediately.
root_cause: API method drift — the script was never re-validated against the current Zenodo REST API. The 504 outage masked the 405 defect because both presented as 'upload failed'.
remediation: Changed upload.ps1 from -Method Post to -Method Put. Re-ran: 23/23 files uploaded successfully (4.81 MB). Verified via the deposition API that all 23 files are present with correct sizes.
impact: Delayed the Zenodo publication. No data corruption. The deposited manuscript is the corrected version (supplyStress 0.17/0.034, matching frozen Phase F evidence).
process_lesson: Distinguish HTTP 4xx (client/method error) from 5xx (server error) before concluding 'the server is down'. A method mismatch never resolves by waiting.
